key_insight: Among WC-10Co-4Cr thermal-sprayed coatings, HVOF and HVAF produce the best overall balance of hardness, low wear, and corrosion resistance, with HVAF slightly leading in corrosion performance.
engineering_relevance: For wear- and corrosion-critical components on stainless steel, spray route selection strongly affects coating density, carbide retention, and service life.
method: WC-10Co-4Cr coatings were deposited on 304 stainless steel using APS, DS, HVOF, and HVAF.
Microstructure, hardness, friction/wear, and electrochemical corrosion behavior were compared across all four processes.
Performance ranking was established from tribology and corrosion tests rather than a single metric.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports hardness increasing from APS to HVOF/HVAF, wear rate dropping from 7.93×10^-5 to about 1.10–1.17×10^-5 mm3/N·m, and HVAF giving the best corrosion metrics (Ecorr = -0.37 VSCE, Icorr = 1.75 μA/cm², Rp = 20438.5 Ω).
watch_item: Results depend on the specific WC-10Co-4Cr system and test conditions, so process rankings may shift with feedstock, substrate, spray parameters, or service environment.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
